title: Redact raw search queries from durable telemetry
description:
Problem: search and context-pack operations can persist raw user query text in the event store. Engineering searches may include customer data, credentials, proprietary symbols, incident details, paths, or pasted code.

Desired outcome: durable telemetry captures useful aggregate diagnostics without retaining raw query content by default.

Scope:
- Store a one-way hash, length, token count, query category, and timing metadata by default.
- Redact obvious secrets and large pasted snippets before any optional diagnostic logging.
- Make raw query capture an explicit short-retention debug option with clear operator controls.
- Apply the policy consistently to lexical, semantic, hybrid, and context-pack paths.
- Out of scope: removing search-quality metrics entirely.

Acceptance criteria:
- Default event records contain no raw query text.
- Equivalent queries can be correlated through a privacy-preserving digest without enabling reversal.
- Optional raw capture is disabled by default, bounded by retention, and clearly documented.
- Tests cover secret-like input, pasted code, empty input, and all search modes.

Validation:
- Run focused search event and telemetry privacy tests.
- Inspect representative event payloads for prohibited raw content.
- Run Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.
